title: Magnets
examples: What kind of things can magnets pull towards them?
How do magnets push things away?
Where are the strong parts of a magnet?

explain.say: A magnet can pull some things towards it. This pull is called attraction.
Now look. This is a bar magnet in 3D. Can you see the north pole and the south pole? Tap any part to hear about it.
Two magnets can also push each other away. This push is called repulsion.
Every magnet has two ends, called poles. One is the north pole, and one is the south pole.
A north pole and a south pole pull together. That is attraction.

draw.text: N pole to S pole: Attract

explain.say: Two north poles push apart. That is repulsion.

draw.text: N pole to N pole: Repel

explain.say: Magnets pull on some materials, like iron and steel. Wood and plastic stay where they are.

faq.q: What materials do magnets like to stick to?
faq.a: Magnets pull on iron and steel. They do not pull wood, plastic, or most other metals, like aluminium.
asks: What can a magnet pick up?

faq.q: Why do magnets push each other away sometimes?
faq.a: Magnets push away when the poles are the same. North pushing North, or South pushing South, will repel.

faq.q: Do magnets have a beginning and an end?
faq.a: Yes, every magnet has two ends called poles. These are always a North pole and a South pole.
asks: What are the ends of a magnet called?
How many poles does a magnet have?

faq.q: Does the magnet have to be big to work?
faq.a: No, even a small magnet can show attraction or repulsion. The poles are what matters most.
asks: Can a small magnet do this?

faq.q: If I mix magnets, what happens?
faq.a: If you put a North pole near a South pole, they will attract. If you put two North poles together, they will repel.
asks: How do I make them stick?

facts: Magnets have two poles: North and South.
Magnets are attracted to magnetic materials like iron.

quiz.say: You put a north pole near a south pole. What happens?
quiz.why: Different poles pull together. That is attraction.

wrong.1: Two poles that are the same push apart.
wrong.2: Magnets close together always pull or push.

quiz.say: Which thing will a magnet pull?
quiz.why: Iron is magnetic, so the magnet pulls the nail.

wrong.0: Wood is not magnetic, so the magnet leaves it.

quiz.say: You push two south poles together. What do you feel?
quiz.why: Poles that are the same push apart. That is repulsion.

wrong.0: Different poles pull together, and these two are the same.
wrong.1: You can feel the two magnets pushing back.
